title: Measuring Honesty Decay as a Function of Conversation Length

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Characterizing the honesty decay curve is useful for monitoring and deployment decisions (trigger warnings at turn thresholds). However, the chain to a safety improvement is indirect: knowing the decay rate does not by itself prevent it.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running multi-turn conversations via API and measuring honest corrections is straightforward. No model training or interpretability tools needed. CS students can implement this with basic API scripting and data analysis.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very tight deliverable: plot of honest correction rate vs. conversation turn count. Well-defined experiment with 4 turn-count conditions and 2 models. Clear output format. 30 hours is comfortable.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is directly and comprehensively addressed by published work. (1) 'TRUTH DECAY: Quantifying Multi-Turn Sycophancy in Language Models' (arXiv:2503.11656, March 2025) is an exact match — it quantifies progressive factual degradation over multiple turns, introduces metrics like Turn of Flip (ToF) and Number of Flip (NoF), and finds up to 40% higher change percentages for initially incorrect answers. (2) 'Measuring Sycophancy of Language Models in Multi-turn Dialogues' (EMNLP 2025 Findings, arXiv:2505.23840) provides additional multi-turn measurement. (3) MIT News (Feb 2026) reports that personalization features increase agreeability over long conversations. The exact research question — plotting honesty against conversation length — has been published with the same title concept ('Truth Decay').
